meta.decision: Fund the second prevention wave starting in Q1 2027
meta.big_idea: Fixing three upstream causes cut denials by a third, and a second wave can repeat that in 2027.
meta.notes: Synthetic example data for the skill self-test. Not real results.

slides.title: Prevention Cut Denials by a Third, and a Second Wave Is Ready
points: Three upstream causes drove most of the gain
Wave two starts in Q1 if funded
slides.notes: Lead with the answer and the ask; the rest of the deck is evidence and plan.

slides.title: Q3 Beat the Goal on All Three Measures
slides.notes: Each measure beat its goal. Write-offs avoided is the number finance asked about.

slides.title: Three Upstream Fixes Did Most of the Work

steps.label: Verify Coverage Earlier
steps.detail: Eligibility runs at scheduling, not at billing

steps.label: Check Authorizations Daily
steps.detail: A daily list flags visits without an authorization

steps.label: Fix Coding at the Source
steps.detail: Top coding errors go back to the clinic weekly

slides.notes: Coverage verification drove about half of the improvement; the other two shared the rest.

slides.title: The Denial Rate Fell by a Third in One Quarter
slides.takeaway: At this rate, prevention pays for wave two within two quarters.
slides.notes: Show the shift, then the payback point. The trend is in the appendix if asked.

slides.title: Prevention Beats Rework Every Time
slides.text: Every denial we prevent is a claim nobody has to touch twice.
slides.notes: Breather: the principle behind the plan that follows.

slides.title: Wave Two Runs January Through June
slides.alt: Roadmap from January to June with prior authorization, coding and training lanes; automated authorization checks highlighted.
slides.notes: Automated authorization checks come first because they are the largest remaining denial cause.

cards.label: Coding Edits
